analysis.title: Happy Fourth Birthday To The Current Bull Market! Does The Rally Have Room To Run Into Year Five?
key_insights: The current bull market is four years old. The S&P 500 has posted a price return of ~117% over that span, above the long-term average of ~90%. All 11 sectors have gained, led by Technology.
Consensus estimates call for S&P 500 EPS to grow 15% in 2027. Raymond James cites this as a supportive backdrop for the bull market to continue.

Median household net worth rose 2% in real terms between 2022 and 2025, reaching $216k, per the Fed's Survey of Consumer Finances. Households in the top 10% of incomes saw net worth rise 31%, while the bottom 40% saw declines.
The wealth gap reflects affluent households benefiting from rising equity and home prices, while persistent inflation pressures lower-income consumers.
Michigan consumer sentiment fell to 46.3 in October, the second-lowest level ever after May's 44.8. The current conditions gauge is at an all-time low.

One-year and five-year inflation expectations each rose 10 bps, to 4.7% and 3.5%. These are the highest levels since May. Raymond James still expects the Fed to hold rates at the October 27-28 meeting.

President Trump said Russia and Ukraine agreed to halt attacks on each other's energy sites. Neither side has confirmed it. The US is lifting sanctions on Russian diesel, but the promised volumes are unlikely to matter much.
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis attacked a major Saudi airport, a sign the Middle East remains volatile.

Earnings season starts tomorrow with Citi, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Wells Fargo, and Financials will stay prominent through the week. UnitedHealth reports tomorrow (read on consumer medical costs), ASML on Wednesday (chip capex), TSMC on Thursday (chip demand) and J.B. Hunt on Thursday (fuel costs).
earnings_insights: Citi, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Wells Fargo report tomorrow (10/13), the first busy day of earnings season. No estimates are given in the report.
UnitedHealth reports tomorrow and is a read on how consumers are handling rising medical costs.
ASML reports Wednesday (10/14) and will address capex in the chip industry.
TSMC reports Thursday (10/15) and will discuss chip demand. J.B. Hunt reports Thursday, with fuel cost management the key question.
Consensus estimates call for S&P 500 EPS growth of 15% in 2027 (forecast).
